_comment: SEVERITY TIER MATRIX for scripts/osint/exposure_score.py (--model tier, and --model actor with exposure_level), documented in analysis/weight-engine.md §10 and handbook/severity-tiers.md. Adapted from the CTI Severity Tier Matrix in [PK Packt ACTIH companion repo, 2026, chapter-01/CTI Severity Tier Matrix.md] (MIT). Two analyst-rated axes read off a fixed grid; a tier is a response priority, never attribution evidence. Vocabulary and thresholds only, never case data (RULE 1).

severities._comment: Axis 1, threat severity, highest first. Rated from the threat itself before looking at our environment; per-trigger patterns are in handbook/severity-tiers.md.

exposures._comment: Axis 2, exposure level, lowest first (the grid column order). 'Negligible' is accepted as an alias of None.

grid._comment: severity row -> [tier at exposure None, Limited, Significant, Extensive]. Design rules checked on load: P1 needs severity >= rules.p1_min_severity AND exposure >= rules.p1_min_exposure; every cell is a tier listed under `tiers` (nothing closes automatically).

rules._comment: p1_min_severity / p1_min_exposure: the lowest row and column where P1 may appear. auto_close false: no cell means 'ignore'.

tiers._comment: tier -> {name, deadline, report_priority, meaning}. P1-P3 deadlines equal the house report's risk_assessment.priorities (exposure_organisation.json); report_priority is the value a key_findings row carries (P1-P4) and, for P1-P3 only, a roadmap row. P4 is track only: no deadline; it may appear as key_findings.priority (rendered 'P4 (track only — no deadline)') but never as a roadmap row.

P1.name: Flash
P1.meaning: act now; advisory to leadership and owners, hunt package, daily tracking

P2.name: Priority
P2.meaning: planned response inside the month; advisory normally issued

P3.name: Standard
P3.meaning: handled in normal work and reviewed for re-tiering

P4.name: Informational
P4.meaning: track only, no deadline; recorded, not closed

axis2_dimensions._comment: The five exposure dimensions the analyst combines into ONE Axis 2 level. Guides only; the combination is analyst judgement and the rationale must say which dimension drove it.

entries.technical: do we run the affected technology, how much of it, and in which critical domains?
entries.targeting: are we inside the sector, region or organisation type the threat goes after?
entries.tradecraft: do our controls cover the techniques involved, or do they land on a gap?
entries.relational: are we tied to victims through a vendor, shared infrastructure, peering or partnership?
entries.detection: would we see this activity class if it were happening here?

retier_triggers._comment: id -> {axis, direction, text}. A re-tier recorded with --case must name one of these ids. Rephrased from upstream; actor_rescored is an adaptation for the actor model.

exploitation_confirmed.text: in-the-wild exploitation or live campaign use is confirmed

new_exposure.text: new exposure surfaces: missed inventory, a new deployment, a newly found vendor tie, a control gap

mitigation_threshold.text: mitigation reaches its threshold: patched, detections live and validated, controls tightened, vendor fixed

actor_adopts.text: an actor of concern takes up the technique or vulnerability, whatever the patch state

sector_shift.text: an actor or campaign moves its targeting into our sector

attribution_downgrade.text: the attacker is reassessed as less capable (for example commodity rather than state-aligned)

actor_rescored.text: (adaptation) the actor's Threat Score crossed a band boundary at a re-score
